description: Implementation map for applying every template context field to generated repository artifacts.

statuses.external: Consumed by callers or Copier routing rather than rendered into files.
statuses.control: Controls whether files or directories are included.
statuses.implemented: Currently rendered into generated project artifacts.
statuses.partial: Currently rendered, but additional relevant artifacts are planned.
statuses.planned: Represented in the contract and reserved for future artifacts.

fields.name: project_name
fields.notes: Rendered into public project titles, citation metadata, and CodeMeta metadata.

fields.name: project_slug
fields.notes: Used wherever the machine-readable project name is required. The contract and finalizer apply scaffold-specific repository or package-name constraints.

fields.name: project_short_description
fields.notes: Short public package description and fallback text for richer metadata.

fields.name: project_long_description
fields.notes: Rendered as optional public motivation and scope prose, with the short description used as a fallback.

fields.name: versioning
fields.notes: Groups the initial version, versioning scheme, optional scheme details, and controlled release frequency. Python uses pyproject.toml and R uses DESCRIPTION as the package version source of truth. Omitted versions use the template's valid technical baseline.

fields.name: development_status
fields.notes: Controlled repostatus.org lifecycle status for machine-readable metadata.

fields.name: keywords
fields.notes: Useful for machine-readable discovery metadata.

fields.name: contributors
fields.notes: Each person declares one or more controlled roles. Original authors and co-authors populate citation and package author metadata; maintainers populate package and citation contact metadata; principal investigators populate leadership metadata. Stable ORCID or URL values are used where supported.

fields.name: funding
fields.notes: Multiple public funding records, including stable funder identifiers and URLs, are rendered as CodeMeta funder/funding metadata and a readable docs overview section.

fields.name: motivation
fields.notes: Groups the public purpose narrative, controlled purpose categories, problem statement, and value proposition.

fields.name: audiences
fields.notes: Intended audiences rendered in human-facing project context.

fields.name: related_software
fields.notes: Related software is rendered as public context and machine-readable CodeMeta relatedLink values when names or links are provided.

fields.name: urls
targets: README CI, docs, and release badges
CodeMeta repository, landing, and help URLs
bio.tools homepage, repository, and documentation links
fields.notes: Groups canonical repository, homepage, and documentation locations while preserving their distinct metadata semantics.

fields.name: registries
fields.notes: Catalogue records support discovery and render as CodeMeta sameAs links when a stable public registry URL can be formed.

fields.name: persistent_identifiers
fields.notes: Supports the CFF identifier types DOI, URL, SWH, and other. CodeMeta contains an explicit replacement placeholder until a persistent identifier is supplied.

fields.name: publications
fields.notes: Associated publications render into concise public notes plus CFF references and CodeMeta referencePublication. A publication marked preferred becomes the CFF preferred-citation and public note.

fields.name: licensing
targets: R MIT license stub and full-text split
Python dependency license compatibility CI workflow
fields.notes: Groups the project license with its dependency-compatibility method. Python supplies automated compatibility tooling; R records the package license and documents the selected method but does not infer an R dependency-license checker.

fields.name: access
fields.notes: Groups the controlled access type with a public explanation or URL. Access is documented separately from the copyright license and mapped to CodeMeta and Schema.org terms.

fields.name: include_metadata
fields.notes: One boolean controls the paired minimum metadata files and their validation workflow.

fields.name: documentation_builder
fields.notes: Python supports Zensical, Sphinx, and MkDocs site generators; omitting the builder produces plain Markdown. R supports pkgdown and otherwise produces plain documentation.

fields.name: documentation_types
fields.notes: The SMP-aligned user, deployment, and developer values drive docs inclusion and page selection. Developer documentation includes technical and API reference material. Empty entries remove the docs scaffold.

fields.name: community_files
fields.notes: Controlled filename selector for standard community files and their directly associated collaboration automation.

fields.name: code_review_policy
fields.notes: Optional public Markdown guidance for reviewer expectations, approvals, and merge conditions. It is rendered only when contributing guidance is selected.

fields.name: support_routes
fields.notes: Multiple public support or issue-reporting systems and URLs, matching the SMP list shape. The first public URL is used as the package issue URL.

fields.name: contacts
fields.notes: Groups public community, code-of-conduct, and private vulnerability-reporting routes.

fields.name: governance_notes
fields.notes: Public governance and decision-making notes.

fields.name: programming_languages
fields.notes: Should include language, version constraint, and role.

fields.name: topics
fields.notes: Project-level research domains expressed as EDAM topic terms; distinct from free-text keywords and function-level EDAM operations.

fields.name: software_functions
targets: bio.tools EDAM functions, inputs, and outputs
fields.notes: Links public EDAM operations to inputs, outputs, command examples, and notes. Function inputs and outputs are the canonical source for format versions, constraints, sample URLs, and supporting-data metadata.

fields.name: interfaces
targets: Python typed runtime configuration for HTTP interfaces
Python configured HTTP server entry point
fields.notes: Controlled public tool types describe how users access the software and select minimal Python scaffolds for common interface families. R generates an exported library API and documents other declared interface families without guessing framework-specific Shiny, plumber, or workflow implementations. HTTP interfaces add validated bind, proxy, reload, and logging settings consumed by one Python server command; FastAPI-backed interfaces can also publish a public base URL. Specification and status are rendered in project documentation; status does not suppress a requested scaffold.

fields.name: operating_systems
fields.notes: Documents all declared platform support. Officially supported Python platforms render into package classifiers, and officially supported Python and R platforms render into their tests CI matrices when they map to GitHub-hosted runners. Both SMP statuses are represented in CodeMeta.

fields.name: external_dependencies
fields.notes: Public external requirements beyond normal language package metadata. Entries render into human-readable docs and CodeMeta softwareRequirements.

fields.name: external_services
fields.notes: Public external services, partners, or roles needed by the project. Entries render into generated documentation only.

fields.name: test_types
fields.notes: SMP checklist labels control test inclusion and which generated sample tests are kept. Empty entries omit the test suite and its CI workflow. Python renders pytest samples; R renders testthat samples and runs R CMD check.

fields.name: test_frameworks
fields.notes: Controlled framework names with template-specific supported choices. Python supports pytest; R supports testthat. Each selection controls native commands, dependency metadata, and CI.

fields.name: quality_tools
fields.notes: Independent controlled formatter, linter, and type-checker properties with template-specific support. Python supports ruff and mypy; R supports styler and lintr.

fields.name: project_manager
targets: R renv setup and lock guidance
fields.notes: One controlled primary manager with template-specific choices. Python supports uv, Poetry, PDM, Hatch, Pixi, and pip. R supports renv and rix, with renv as the empty-selection fallback.

fields.name: distribution_channels
fields.notes: Python automates PyPI, GitHub Releases, and selected container registries. R builds checked source packages for CRAN, Bioconductor, and GitHub Releases; review-driven submissions remain external. Zenodo generates shared release metadata.

fields.name: containerization
fields.notes: Python and R generate native Docker, OCI/Podman, and Apptainer/Singularity recipes. Project managers and their lockfiles are controlled independently.

fields.name: resource_requirements
targets: README fallback when docs are omitted
fields.notes: Public typical and worst-case memory, storage, compute, GPU, wall-clock, and scaling expectations.

fields.name: maintenance_level
fields.notes: Controlled public support and maintenance commitment after active development.

fields.name: continuity_plan
fields.notes: Public handover or continuity notes.

fields.name: retirement_criteria
fields.notes: Public criteria for archival or retirement.

fields.name: public_risk_notes
fields.notes: Public risk notes only; sensitive detail belongs elsewhere.

fields.name: regulatory_requirements
fields.notes: One object combines controlled SMP compliance choices with an optional public free-text complement.

fields.name: security_measures
fields.notes: One object combines controlled public security measures with an optional public free-text complement. Python adds typed configuration and vulnerability automation for applicable selections; R renders the public policy without guessing an ecosystem security scanner.

fields.name: data_management
fields.notes: Groups the public sensitive-data statement with the public DMP reference or contact route.
